chunks: Surely those who fear God and follow the straight path will be amidst gardens and fresh springs of water,

key_terms.الْمُتَّقِينَ: The pious; those who fear God and follow His commands
key_terms.جَنَّاتٍ: Gardens; plural of Jannah, referring to Paradise
key_terms.عُيُونٍ: Springs; plural of Ayn, referring to flowing water sources in Paradise

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for the Muttaqeen in the afterlife according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Adh-Dhariyat is often linked with its preceding context to emphasize that the 'springs' (Uyun) refer not only to physical rivers but also to the intellectual and spiritual clarity granted to the righteous. This dual interpretation underscores the Shia emphasis on both material reward and the purification of the soul through divine knowledge (Ma'rifah). The promise serves as a consolation for the faithful who endure trials, affirming that piety leads to eternal serenity in the presence of God.
